title: Grateful Dead Live at Barton Hall on 1977-05-08
source: source: aud taped by Jerry Moore; 1)cassette master>10.5" reel @ 7.5 ips, dolby b provides a majority of the show, 2)Scarlet>Fire provided by cassette master patched from same rig>JM's cassette>reel (as above); 3)The One More Sat Nite encore is from the newly discovered original cassette master; lineage for source 1 (with exceptions noted above): aud cassette master: sony ecm 33p's>sony tc-153, maxell udxLII90's/dolby b>aud 1st gen: made on Sony TC-755 w/Teac an-180 dolby unit, Scotch Classic 10.5" reels; transfer: technics rs-1506 open reel>teac an-180 dolby b unit>tascam hd-p2 24/96>flac encore: nak dragon>tascam hd-p2 24/96>pc>flac; new transfers by Rob Berger spring 2011; mastering, pitch correction, and seeded by Charlie Miller

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording with a sparkling 'Loser' solo and second‑set highlights like 'Dancin’ in the Streets', despite ongoing debates about its authenticity.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑mastered soundboard source is crisp, well‑balanced and benefits from careful audience patches, making the tape sound almost studio‑quality. Musically the show shines on the second half – Scarlet Begonias → Fire, a killer 'Loser' solo, 'Dancin’ in the Streets' and a standout Brown Eyed Women – while some listeners feel the first set drifts a bit. Overall the performance is praised by most fans, even if a few still argue the concert never really happened.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (≈15 out of 18) give 4‑5 stars and praise both the audio quality and musical moments; only a few raise authenticity concerns or critique the first set, resulting in a strong positive consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Miller mastering praised as 'splendid', clean SB patches, occasional high‑mid harshness that could use gentle EQ; audience patches blend well and overall the tape is crisp and balanced.

standout_songs: Scarlet Begonias > Fire on the Mountain
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set described as a little sleepy, but the second set picks up dramatically with St Stephen leading into a high‑energy stretch of Scarlet Begonias → Fire and a soaring Dancin’ in the Streets.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His solo on 'Loser' is repeatedly highlighted as exceptional.
